How much does the draft decide?: How much does the draft decide?
Once both teams are locked in, how well: Once both teams are locked in, how well do the ten champions predict who wins?
We compared four models with a baseline: We compared four models with a baseline that always picks the blue side: one number per team (the sum of each champion's patch win rate), team make-up, a rating per champion, and boosted trees. Games come from players who chose to share them, with names removed. Every score is measured on games the model hadn't seen (5-fold cross-validation, repeated 10 times), with 95% ranges.
The draft matters, a little. The best mo: The draft matters, a little. The best model gets 60% of games right against 54% for always picking blue, and its AUC is 0.61 (95% range 0.58 to 0.65, where 0.50 is a coin flip). Shuffling the results and retraining beats it about 1 time in 300. The simplest model won: one number per team did as well as the detailed ones. Where the draft edge is clearest (a third of games) the favourite wins about 64%; in the closest third, 55%.
1,081 games is a small sample for a five: 1,081 games is a small sample for a five-versus-five game, so the ranges are wide, and they come from a small group of players. The model ignores augments, items and skill on purpose. We rerun it as more games arrive.

Changes are also sized as Mayhem modifiers, to estimate what each kind of change is worth.

A win rate also moves for reasons the no: A win rate also moves for reasons the notes don't list, such as item and augment changes, new tricks and hotfixes. Many changes bundle several lines, so the value of each kind is rough, and small changes can't be told from noise.
